title: A literature review Health systems adaptation proposals to address the combined impacts of climate change, food insecurity and conflict: a literature review
content:
Abstract
Climate change, food insecurity, and conflict (CFC) represent a critical intersection of issues impacting global health systems, particularly in fragile and conflict-affected settings. This literature review synthesizes evidence from five studies published between 2021 and 2024, highlighting global health vulnerabilities and health system level adaptive strategies in the face of CFC challenges. Climate change exacerbates health risks through extreme weather events, rising temperatures, and resource depletion, often aggravating food insecurity and triggering or intensifying conflicts. These phenomena synergistically amplify health crises, including malnutrition, epidemics, and reduced access to care. The researchers conducted a rapid literature review to scope the coverage of this issue and documented the impacts of this trilemma, such as heightened incidence of stunting and wasting among children, increase in food- and waterborne diseases, injuries and heat-related conditions among others. Our findings underscore the necessity of integrating disaster-health preparedness, conflict-sensitive approaches, and cost-effective practices into adaptation frameworks. A systematic gap in current policies was identified, where climate change, food security, and conflict are rarely addressed holistically within health system planning. Additionally, the findings emphasize the importance of aligning immediate humanitarian responses with long-term resilience-building, prioritizing evidence-based planning, equitable resource distribution, and multisectoral engagement. By addressing the CFC trilemma cohesively, health systems can better mitigate risks and enhance adaptive capacities. This review highlights the urgent need for global and local stakeholders to collaborate in bridging the gaps in research and practice, ensuring that health systems are equipped to respond to the complex and interlinked challenges of climate change, food insecurity, and conflict.
